brief:
A new documentary explores how perpetrators of mass atrocities justify their involvement, according to The Guardian, challenging the assumption that genocide is committed only by sadists and brutish individuals. The film examines how people who are otherwise recognizable as ordinary explain their participation in extreme violence, using the example of Werner Best, a senior SS official and legal administrator who helped organize Nazi death squads.

The documentary suggests that modern genocides are sustained not by exceptional monsters but by individuals capable of constructing rational-seeming explanations for their actions. This framing complicates how societies typically understand perpetrators of mass violence, shifting focus from character pathology to the mechanics of psychological and ideological justification.

title: Ordinary people rationalize participation in genocide, documentary shows
